 Syracuse men’s basketball: predictions and poll vs St John’s
 Back in the Mecca!
 by Kevin Wall , Dominic Chiappone , Max Cohen , Sam Federman , and James Szuba Nov 15, 2026, 4:00 PM UTC Facebook 
 Link 
 It’s a primetime matchup from Madison Square Garden tonight as the Syracuse Orange (2-1) look to make their first statement under Gerry McNamara. Waiting for the Orange in the World’s Most Famous Arena are Rick Pitino’s #13 St. John’s Red Storm (3-0).
 Tip-off tonight is 7:00 and the game is airing on Peacock. Here’s what we’re predicting:
 Kevin: St. John’s 88, Syracuse 74 
 I don’t think the Orange can slow the game down enough to stay within range, and without Tobiason and possibly Morano I don’t think they can score enough to stay within range. Taking care of the ball, getting on the glass and getting to the foul line is the recipe that Syracuse will need to grab a massive win in MSG.
 Max: St. John’s 84, Syracuse 69 
 St. John’s has looked great in their first three wins, and unfortunately Syracuse won’t be stopping that. The passing execution is gonna be too much to handle for the Orange at MSG and they will be adding a quality loss to the resume instead of the preferred upset win.
 Dom: St. John’s 79, Syracuse 62 
 Yeah, this is gonna be a rough one and there’s no way around it. This is a very good Rick Pitino-led squad. If the Orange had Tobiason, I think that would certainly change things. But I’m incredibly worried about the offense going up against the Johnnies’ defense. If Syracuse goes to more scoring-focused groups, the Tounde Yessoufou, Ian Jackson, and Quinn Ellis trio will collectively light up the Syracuse backcourt. Syracuse leaves MSG with its first double-digit defeat of the season.
 Sam: St. John’s 87, Syracuse 71 
 I just think that St. John’s is going to overpower Syracuse with speed and pressure. This game will be too fast for Syracuse’s liking, and the Johnnies will control the tempo and the flow of what lineups Syracuse will have to play. If Indiana’s guards gave SU trouble, then St. John’s certainly will too.
 Szuba: St. John’s 85, Syracuse 72 
 St. John’s is the more talented team here and while I think Syracuse can hang offensively, the rebounding from the Orange has left much to be desired thus far. Hard to think Syracuse can get the defensive stops it needs against a team of athletes. The Pitino full-court press is a new kind of challenge for this Syracuse team. Although the Orange have the depth, it’s asking a lot of off-ball guys like Anthony, Doty and Morano to handle the ball, execute in the half court and play defense. St John’s with a double-digit win.
